messages.author: d3397caecb538f6f
messages.subject: Mixing in ODE model
parts:
Hi everybody,

I am trying to fit a model based on differential equations against experimental time courses using RSTAN. When running more chains in parallel, some chains seem to get stuck into different regions of the parameter space (I attach a traceplot as an example). 
I was wondering how I can improve mixing.
Thank you for your attention.

Best,

Daniele

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Mixing in ODE model
parts:
ODE models are notorious for be non-identified — especially
when the data are sparse there end up being many parameters
consistent with the measurements.  This is especially likely
when you have unobserved states in the system of ODEs.

Because the model is fundamentally multimodal, there’s not 
much you can do besides change the model or add data,
especially to unobserved components.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Mixing in ODE model
parts:
It looks like it's mixing around modes rather than getting stuck
at a single value. If you rerun, do you get the same modes?

Alternatively, if you can somehow deduce one of the modes has almost
all of the probability mass (not density), then you can initialize
around that mode with a small step size and you'll stay near it.
You can sometimes achieve this naturally with an appropriate prior.

- Bob

messages.author: d3397caecb538f6f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Mixing in ODE model
parts:
Dear Michael and Bob,

Thank you very much for your feedback.
I have re-run STAN using 5 chains with the control parameter

control=list(adapt_delta=0.9)

I attach the traceplots together with the file with the model definition.

Two chains seem to mix around the same mode (chain 1 and chain 3), chain 4 seems to mix around a different mode, chain 2 and chain 5 are stuck at a single value.

The model is defined by 6 ODEs and depends on 6 variables (C_B, V_B, C_A, V_A, C_C, V_C). The values in time of each of these variables are fitted against experimental time courses (6 experimental time courses in total). The model is quite minimal for this dataset and I wouldn’t expect major changes in the model or in the experimental data.
 
It seems there are two issues. One might be related to multi-modality and the other to poor mixing. As regards chains that are mixing well but around different modes, would it be more appropriate to consider the parameters inferred by all chains or select a chain (chains) based on the “lp__” term in Stan’s output and re-run STAN reducing the prior around the parameter values inferred by that chain (those chains)?
As regards the chains that are stuck, how can I improve mixing? Can I neglect them if they don’t mix well?
Thank you again.

Best,

Daniele

messages.author: 3d7541308bd2e290
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Mixing in ODE model
parts:
Have you made a generated quantities block and looked at the posterior predictives? That's what I'd do in a situation like this.

The reason I'm asking is it seems strange that the 'sigma_fit' parameter would be multimodal (and 3.0 vs 5.0 seems like a big difference). If I'm reading your model correctly, it's saying:

C ~ normal(ode, sigma_fit)
V ~ normal(ode, sigma_fit)

So I think this is the sort of modeling you'd do if you have measurement noise, and, if it is measurement noise, hopefully it corresponds to the precision of some instrument, which hopefully only has one precision (and maybe someone might have a vague idea what it should be too). It also seems weird that two processes (C and V) have the same noise level as well.

Anyway, it's probably worth doing a generated quantities and just checking which modes explain your data better and going from there.

I wouldn't try to read too much into the log probabilities thing.

Ben

Thank you very much for your reply; I’ll account for the posterior predictive distributions together with the lp__ value.

The data are derived from the concentration levels of a biomarker in an intestinal tissue of different mice and it is difficult to estimate the measurement noise a priori.
C and V are two compartments of the same experimental measurements and I would expect a similar noise level.
Thanks again,

Daniele
